title: feat(nfexist): existential opposite neighbor-lock: reverse fail, face holds
science: Existential-opposite predicate (some a in S(A), b in S(B) with a+b=0) on lock SETS: S(A)={+e_1}, S(B)={+e_1,+e_3}, S(C)={-e_2}, S(D)={+e_2} -> reverse FAIL, face HOLD. Duplicates collapse and mixed lists stay defined, so this is a third way to handle B's mixture; the note tabulates that unique-vector gives reverse UNDEFINED and sum gives reverse fail `for a different reason`.
